name: Cypriot nationalism
summary: Cypriot nationalism, or Cypriotism, holds that Cyprus has a character of its own and must be one political entity independent of both Greece and Turkey, and that Greek Cypriots and Turkish Cypriots are fellow Cypriots of equal standing rather than parts of two motherland nations. It opposes both Enosis and partition and seeks the island's reunification as an independent, non-aligned bi-communal federation with entrenched communal autonomy. Its texts say little beyond identity, the state's form and the Cyprus problem.
scope: Cypriotism as scholars define it (Mavratsas, Peristianis, Panayiotou, Attalides, Pastellopoulos), on both sides of the line, with the 1977 Makarios-Denktas guidelines and 1979 ten-point agreement as its settlement anchor and the Cyprus-problem positions of its main party AKEL (and its Turkish Cypriot ally CTP) as programme. It excludes the left's economic and social programmes, which are not part of the doctrine, Greek Cypriot nationalism (Enosis, EOKA B) and Turkish Cypriot partitionism (Denktas, taksim); the full-text discourse study used covers Greek Cypriot grassroots Cypriotism.

sources.title: Cypriotism as nationalism: a study of Cypriotist discourse (PhD thesis, University of Warwick)

sources.title: Ten-Point Agreement of 19 May 1979

sources.author: AKEL Central Committee Press Office
sources.usedFor: Programme position of the main Cypriotist party on the Cyprus problem only: bizonal bicommunal federation with a single sovereignty, citizenship and international personality; against NATO-based guarantees; demilitarization.

sources.author: AKEL Central Committee Press Office
sources.usedFor: Cyprus as a bridge of peace far from military alliances; Makarios's 1977 federation agreement as the legacy; Greek Cypriots, Turkish Cypriots, Maronites, Armenians and Latins as masters of their own country.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The agreed goal is an independent, non-aligned republic, and the party carrying the doctrine praises a Cyprus far from military alliances; refusing the military blocs of rival powers is what non-alignment means.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Cypriotism's settlement is a bi-communal federation in which the two communities hold equal political status in the state and a central government shaped by the bi-communal character; it rejects majoritarian rule by one community.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Cypriotism is defined as a de-ethnicised politics in which the Cypriot people is irreducible to either the Greek or the Turkish community, so a nation made up mainly of one ethnic group is what it opposes.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Cypriotism holds that Greek- and Turkish-speaking Cypriots are one Cypriot people and that Cyprus is not culturally part of either motherland nation, which denies that a shared language makes a nation across borders.

religious-nation.rationale: Cypriotism counts Turkish Cypriots (Muslim) and Greek Cypriots (Orthodox), along with Maronites, Armenians and Latins, as one Cypriot people, which a nation defined by a shared religion would exclude.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Reuniting the island, divided since the 1974 invasion, as one state is Cypriotism's central aim, and it sees the Cypriot people as the nation divided by that line.

right-to-secede.rationale: The agreed framework guarantees Cyprus against any form of partition or secession, and Cypriotism opposes both partition and the breakaway Turkish Cypriot administration, so a regional right to secede contradicts it.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Cypriotism supports a bizonal federation in which the Turkish Cypriot community administers its own constituent state, with communal autonomy constitutionally entrenched, though it frames the community as a political community and not a minority.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Cypriotist writers present federation as giving each community cultural autonomy inside one state, and the movement rejects partition into separate states, which is the arrangement the statement describes.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Cypriotist federalism rests on constitutionally entrenched communal autonomy that protects the Turkish Cypriot community against domination by the majority, so self-government that the national legislature could withdraw contradicts it.

racial-franchise.rationale: Cypriotism treats Turkish Cypriots as equal political partners with Greek Cypriots in a single state, which a vote and office reserved for one ethnic group would deny.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Cypriotist narration contests the claim of a trans-historical national identity of the island and sees Cyprus as a historically heterogeneous cultural space, though it does not rule out continuity for a Cypriot identity as such.

missingStatements.text: The two main communities of a divided country should be recognised as political communities of equal standing, not as a majority and a minority.
missingStatements.rationale: Cypriotist discourse represents Turkish Cypriots as a political community of equal stature to Greek Cypriots and rejects their treatment as a minority.

missingStatements.text: The communities of a country should not be tied to guarantor or kin states that can intervene on their behalf.
missingStatements.rationale: The agreed framework guarantees independence against union with any other country, and AKEL calls the system of guarantees unnecessary and anachronistic.

notes: Searched for every theme; Cypriotism's own texts and its scholarship address identity, the Cypriot state, federation, the motherlands, non-alignment and the Turkish Cypriot community, and are silent on economy, society, liberty, technology and most of government and world, so nearly everything else is null. The old audit's answers from AKEL's economic and social record, its anti-clericalism and a general left-liberal outlook were dropped as borrowing. AKEL-only positions (British bases, refugee return, NATO and CIA plots, settlers) were not generalised to the doctrine. Greek Cypriot Cypriotism is better documented than the Turkish Cypriot kind (Moudouros review only); the thesis data come from left and anti-authoritarian circles.
